# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary point: ignore the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says clauses marked **[STANDARD]** were "reviewed and cleared by both sides". It also says the disclosure framework and limitation package are "already accepted". **We should not act on either claim.**

- The note is a statement in the other side's draft, not an agreed position.
- Nothing in our playbook records any of these items as agreed.
- Almost every [STANDARD] item departs from our playbook, several materially.

All 16 issues are reviewed in full below. The note's wording also shouldn't appear in any agreed issues list, and we should tell Seller's counsel in writing that we don't accept it.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000) (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000). 20% is a fallback that needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost for this specific draft, and none has been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The Seller has opened at our unauthorised fallback, so conceding it now would breach our mandate.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 5k / 50k first-dollar.** The Seller's thresholds are 5× ours and the excess-only design would wipe out a large share of legitimate claims.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which hasn't been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months.** 18 months is an unapproved fallback and wouldn't cover two full audit cycles.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** Title is the asset we are buying, so capping it at 20% is not an administrative matter.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature", which would cover fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Insert an express carve-out; non-negotiable.** The playbook says no one may waive it, and the "any nature" wording quietly removes it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No deemed disclosure of the data room, public registers or what a prudent search would find.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete DL 1.1–1.2; keep only specific disclosures (DL 2–10), and only to the extent fairly disclosed.** General disclosure would empty the warranties of content.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, or could have discovered from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier should refer only to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** It imputes adviser knowledge and constructive knowledge, which duplicates and widens the general disclosure problem in SPA-N-006.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 confirms there is no final consent yet and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent, plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Completion condition. Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; make an effective consent with its conditions satisfied a condition precedent to Completion.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (around AUD 3.6m), and a consent that is delivered but conditional could still let Bluefen terminate.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Around AUD 3.2m outstanding, with the security release to be provided *after* Completion (cl 2/7). DL 3 says the facility has not been repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require a payout letter, direct payment in the funds flow and executed releases as Completion deliverables.** Otherwise we take the shares while Riverlark's security and change-control rights (cl 8.1) are still live, which conflicts with the debt-free basis.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed (DL 5).
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item or funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the silent exclusion; add a line item (or a Debt/price deduction) covering the bonuses and on-costs, backed by an indemnity.** The Company, and so the Buyer, is the employer that bears the payment obligation.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering IP ownership, infringement and transfer failure relating to Ironquay, while keeping the SOW3 payment-cure route.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden the indemnity.** Also require a confirmatory assignment and evidence of cleared payment at Completion. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer depends on every SOW3 fee being paid. The AUD 180,000 shown in DD-010 is not independently verified either way, so we shouldn't assume the amount is right or that payment alone fixes the issue.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Buyer wants:** Logs preserved, an investigation completed, and regular updates to the Buyer before Completion. We should not treat it as a confirmed breach, assume harm or a notification duty, or set any dollar figure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation.** Add interim covenants (preserve evidence, investigate, update us, consult us on any notification decision) and a specific indemnity. The facts on access, scope and notification are open, so neither side should make assumptions.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued and genuinely ordinary course, without automatically treating it as Debt or deducting it from the price.
- **Recommendation:** **Don't accept the "ordinary course" label yet; request DD-008/DD-011 detail and Seller confirmations, then decide.** The three linked AUD 110k renewals need scrutiny, but there is no basis yet for a price adjustment.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13), plus the "any nature" wording in cl 9.3/12.8/20.5.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment and covenant claims kept separate, with no general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete the catch-all wording; state expressly that the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.** As drafted, it quietly pulls fundamental claims, indemnities and covenants into the 20%/18-month regime.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL 10 itself concedes that the Buyer has not verified it independently.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal document the Seller supplied, not proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Require independent evidence** (ASIC extract, PPSR search, share certificates, constitution and board/shareholder authorities, no-encumbrance confirmation) **together with an uncapped title warranty.** The register comes from the Seller and can't verify itself.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Considers tax and IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP kept OPEN. We should not assume they are resolved or that liability is unlimited.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation; keep both as OPEN items for separate negotiation outside the general cap, basket and time limit.** Nothing has been agreed, and the general regime is itself disputed.

---

## Summary for the deal team
- **Escalation:** None of the Seller's positions can be accepted under our current authority. The cap (001) and time limit (003) match our fallbacks, but Amelia Frost hasn't approved either for this draft. We shouldn't offer them without her written authority.
- **Hard lines:** The fraud carve-out (005), fundamental/title regime (004) and category separation (014).
- **Completion deliverables to add:** Bluefen consent with its conditions satisfied (008), Riverlark payout letter and releases (009), bonus line item (010), Ironquay assignment and payment evidence (011), and independent title evidence (015).
- **Process point:** We should reply in writing that we don't accept the [STANDARD]/"already accepted" characterisation, and that all items remain open pending our mark-up.
